label: Reading Aquinas’s participation commentary
summary: The pinned Turin 1954 lectio 2 distinguishes particular-to-universal, subject-to-accident or matter-to-form, and effect-to-cause participation. Aquinas’s effect-to-cause example is the same air receiving the sun’s light below the brightness it has in the sun. The same analysis cannot be read as assigning a single potency-to-act relation to all three kinds.
blocker: Determine which modes fall under ParticipatesIn and show that the participant itself is the potency receiving the same perfection for every relevant ReceivedIn instance.
